title: Normalized inverse-limit comparisons respect an exact functor square
statement:
For $i=0,1,2,3$, let $\mathcal C_i$ be a site small in the module universe, $R_i$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A_i=\operatorname{Mod}(R_i)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in each $\mathcal A_i$ are exact. Let $F:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal A_1$, $G:\mathcal A_1\to\mathcal A_3$, $H:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal A_2$, and $K:\mathcal A_2\to\mathcal A_3$ be additive exact functors whose canonical countable-product comparisons $\phi_E:E(\prod_nN_n)\to\prod_nE(N_n)$ are invertible. Let $e:GF\xrightarrow{\sim}KH$ be a natural isomorphism. Use the same letters for termwise functors on complexes and strict towers and their exact derived functors [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Write $L_i=R\lim$ on $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_i))$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use precisely the comparisons $\lambda_E$ and normalized isomorphisms $\theta:L_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf R_i$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], with signed coordinates
$$\mathsf R_i(M)^q=P_M^q\oplus P_M^{q-1},\quad P_M=\prod_nM_n,\quad d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy).$$

For any countable family $(N_n)$ in $\mathcal A_0$ and $P=\prod_nN_n$, the prescribed product maps satisfy
$$(\prod_ne_{N_n})\circ\phi_G\circ G(\phi_F)
=\phi_K\circ K(\phi_H)\circ e_P.$$
Their common composite has $n$th projection $e_{N_n}\circ GF(\pi_n)=KH(\pi_n)\circ e_P$. Let $\kappa_E:E\mathsf R_i\to\mathsf R_jE$ be the canonical biproduct comparison followed by $\phi_E$ on both signed summands. For every strict tower complex $M$, one has the chain-map equality
$$\mathsf R_3(e_M)\circ\kappa_{G,FM}\circ G(\kappa_{F,M})
=\kappa_{K,HM}\circ K(\kappa_{H,M})\circ e_{\mathsf R_0M}.$$
This equality descends to the derived categories. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_0))$ the normalized comparisons obey
$$L_3(e_M)\circ\lambda_{G,FM}\circ G(\lambda_{F,M})
=\lambda_{K,HM}\circ K(\lambda_{H,M})\circ e_{L_0M}.$$
This is natural for all derived tower maps, with $e$ localized termwise and $\lambda_E=\theta_{EM}^{-1}\kappa_{E,M}E(\theta_M)$, including its specified K-injective normalization.

For every complex $C$ and strict augmentation $\gamma:\Delta C\to M$ [def-weil-inverse-system], the composite $\lambda_G\circ G(\lambda_F)$ carries $GF(u_\gamma)$ to $u_{GF\gamma}$, and $\lambda_K\circ K(\lambda_H)$ carries $KH(u_\gamma)$ to $u_{KH\gamma}$. Here $u$ is the canonical derived augmentation map specified in [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. These maps satisfy $L_3(e_M)\circ u_{GF\gamma}=u_{KH\gamma}\circ e_C$. No functor is assumed to preserve K-injective objects, and no boundedness is imposed.

proof.text: Construct one common localized roosF at each corner, using the generic roos_map_quasiIso and roos_universal proofs of StrictRoosDerivation. For independent coefficient universes obtain moduleSheaves_grothendieck and tower_grothendieck from RingedStrictTowerHomotopyLimitIndependentCoefficients. Uniqueness of right derived functors supplies theta, and its unit equation gives eta_X followed by theta and the factorization equal to Q(roosι_X), for every X (hence also for the prescribed injective complexes). The choices here are localization and derived universal objects, not arbitrary witnesses of an unproved existence statement.

proof.text: Use the actual roosAdditiveComparison for each edge. Its product-preservation hypothesis follows from invertibility of all piComparison maps. Its two coordinate equations, after the fixed braiding and negation, give the exact signed formula in Comparison. Lift its natural isomorphism through fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft; the preimage equation gives descent. Define lambda by conjugating this derived comparison with the shared corner theta maps.

proof.text: Apply product projection uniqueness. Pi.map and piComparison reduce each nth projection to GF(pi_n) followed by e_Nn. Naturality of e at pi_n gives the other path. This proves product_square, product_projection and projection_naturality without a preservation assumption on the product calculation itself.

proof.text: Form both derived natural transformations. Localization.natTrans_ext reduces equality to Q(X). Postcompose by the invertible target tower factorization followed by the corner factorization. The exact-functor composition and natural-isomorphism factor equations, naturality of corner factors, and the two edge descents reduce to Q of the chain square. This proves the Roos square on every derived object and morphism. Substitute the four conjugation equations, cancel theta_1 and theta_2, and use naturality of theta_3 and the localized e to obtain normalized_square.

proof.text: The strict augmentation is limit.lift(gamma) followed by roosι. The existing Roos augmentation equation identifies it with roosAugment(gamma), and roosAdditiveComparison_augmentation carries it to the mapped cone augmentation. Use the edge descent and the unit normalization from the first step, cancel the target normalization, and obtain one-edge augmentation compatibility. Apply it successively for F,G and H,K to prove augmentationFG and augmentationHK.

proof.text: Naturality of eta_3 at the explicitly typed termwise square map reduces augmentation_square to equality of strict maps into the limit. Test on every tower projection and every complex degree. The remaining equality is exactly e.naturality at gamma_n^q. Thus the actual canonical strict augmentation is respected, without boundedness or preservation of injectives.
